title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core positioning, competitive brief templates, recommended pitch deck structure, pricing guidance, short case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Intended audience: SDRs/AE/solutions engineers and product-marketing partners preparing customer-facing materials or competitive responses.

Purpose:
- Provide a single reference for consistent messaging across sales motions (self-serve, mid-market, enterprise).
- Equip reps with quick competitive counters and quantified value props.
- Standardize pitch decks and pricing deskside guidance to accelerate deal cycles.

1) Core Positioning & Messaging (elevator + supporting bullets)
- Elevator (15–30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes production-grade LLM serving predictable and cost‑efficient across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Problem we solve: Teams struggle to reliably run LLMs at production scale while balancing latency, cost, and compliance.
- Primary benefits (customer-facing):
  - Predictable performance: low tail latency (p99 SLOs), dedicated capacity options, and per-route observability.
  - Cost control: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce unit token costs (typical customers see 30–60% reduction vs unmanaged serving).
  - Deployment flexibility: hosted API for fast time-to-value, Reserved/Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private/VPC for regulated workloads.
  - Reliability & graceful degradation: smart routing and model-variant fallbacks keep apps online under load.
- Evidence & differentiators:
  - Benchmark highlights: curated model catalog with verified latency profiles; example: 8k-context Llama-3-x on A100 — median generation latency 80ms/token under continuous batching.
  - Enterprise features: SLA-backed Dedicated, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2 Type II evidence, and audit logs for private deployments.

2) Competitive Briefs (template + top rivals and counters)
- Use this template in competitive calls:
  1. One-line summary of competitor position.
  2. Typical customer need where competitor wins.
  3. Where Redwood differentiates (concrete evidence).
  4. Suggested rebuttal + customer-fit questions.
- Short competitor notes:
  - Major Cloud Provider Endpoints (GCP/AWS/Azure managed endpoints):
    - Strengths: deep cloud integration, broad managed services, account stickiness.
    - Redwood counters: superior token-level observability, inference-specific runtime kernels, unified API across hosted/dedicated/private for easier multi‑cloud/multi‑env rollouts.
    - Rebuttal question: "How do you currently measure per-route token costs and regressions across model upgrades?"
  - LLM API-focused vendors (simplicity-first providers):
    - Strengths: very simple APIs, strong developer UX at experiment stage.
    - Redwood counters: when apps move to production these customers need SLOs, predictable costs, and private deployment options — areas where Redwood is built for the post-prototype phase.
  - Self-hosted inference runtimes (open-source or managed infra vendors):
    - Strengths: full control and potentially lower infra cost at large scale.
    - Redwood counters: we provide production-grade serving runtime optimized for latency and batching, plus orchestration and operations (rollouts, canaries, tracing) that reduce run‑time engineering overhead.

3) Pitch Deck Guidance (recommended structure and slide-level talking points)
- Recommended 10–12 slide deck flow for initial enterprise outreach:
  1. Title + value headline (1 line): "Predictable LLM inference for production—lower cost, lower latency, enterprise-ready"
  2. Problem & market context (developer velocity vs ops complexity)
  3. Redwood value props (3 bullets: performance, cost, deployments)
  4. How it works (runtime + smart routing + caching) — simple architecture diagram (text alt: "Serving runtime -> Router -> Dedicated/GPU pool -> Private/VPC")
  5. Deployment modes & when to choose each (hosted, dedicated, private)
  6. Performance & cost benchmarks (one slide: median latency, p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens delta vs unmanaged)
  7. Security & compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs)
  8. Customer case study (same as in this doc)
  9. Pricing & commercial options (summary, see Pricing Guidance)
  10. Rollout plan & success criteria (pilot → scale)
  11. Next steps / ask (pilot proposal, technical POC, contract)
- Slide tips for SEs/AEs: include concrete numbers (latency, cost savings) and an explicit pilot statement: "2–4 week pilot, defined eval prompts, stop/rollback criteria, POA for security review".

4) Pricing Guidance (sales-facing summary)
- Pricing motion overview:
  - Self-serve / Hosted: usage-based pricing (per-token generation + embedding units). Ideal for proofs-of-concept and early-stage product flows.
  - Dedicated: committed monthly/annual reserved capacity. Pricing tiers depend on GPU class (e.g., A100 vs H100), reserved vCPU/GPU counts, and provisioned concurrency.
  - Private: platform fee + deployment services for VPC/on-prem plus optional support SLAs.
- Quick commercial heuristics for deals:
  - SMB / startup: prefer hosted usage; watch for steady-state > $10–15k/month — trigger AE outreach for Dedicated proposal.
  - Mid-market: typical progression is hosted POC → Dedicated reservation with 12–24 month commit once latency & throughput are validated.
  - Enterprise: expect security review, private deployment, and multi-quarter procurement. Engage solutions engineering and legal early.
- Discount guardrails: standard term-based discounts (10–25%) for 12–36 month commitments; deeper discounts tied to minimum committed spend and multi-year onboarding plans.

5) Case Studies (two concise examples for sales use)
- Case study A — Conversational SaaS (mid-market)
  - Problem: Customer faced erratic latency and 3–4x higher token spend after moving from prototype to production.
  - Solution: Redwood Dedicated + batching, prefix caching, and quantization profile.
  - Outcome (30-day): 45% lower per-token cost; p99 latency improved from 1.2s to 0.35s under typical traffic; time-to-detect regressions reduced by 5 days using per-route eval hooks.
  - Contactable reference: marketing@redwood.example (internal: ref-id CS-2025-17)
- Case study B — Regulated Enterprise (finance)
  - Problem: Strict data residency and audit requirements prevented using public endpoints.
  - Solution: Private deployment (VPC + KMS integration) with dedicated control plane and audit logging.
  - Outcome (90-day): Contract renewal secured after pilot; vendor consolidation reduced vendor sprawl; compliance review passed with minor remediation items.
  - Contactable reference: enterprise-customer-success@redwood.example (internal: ref-id CS-2025-22)

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (short answers to common questions)
- Q: Do you SOC2 / ISO certifications?
  - A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001; SOC2 report is available under NDA.
- Q: How do you handle customer keys and secrets?
  - A: Customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations supported for Private deployments; Hosted customers may use Redwood-managed keys with optional BYOK for enterprise tiers.
- Q: Is data stored from inference requests?
  - A: By default hosted customers can opt-in to temporary caching for cost/perf; data retention and logging policies are configurable. Private deployments leave data residency to the customer.
- Q: How do you support audit and compliance needs?
  - A: Audit logs, access trail, SSO + SCIM, RBAC, and integration hooks for SIEM available; compliance packages and evidence bundles provided for enterprise deals.
- Q: What is your incident response posture?
  - A: 24x7 incident response for enterprise SLAs, documented playbooks, and root-cause reports for Sev1 incidents.

7) Sales Playbook: Deal-stage checklist (pilot → negotiate → close)
- Pilot (technical validation)
  - Define success criteria and evaluation prompt set (owner: AE + SE).
  - Provision sandbox (hosted or dedicated trial capacity).
  - Run perf & quality evaluations; deliver report within 10 business days.
- Negotiation
  - Present recommended pricing tier tied to observed capacity.
  - Provide security evidence bundle and legal standard terms.
- Close & Onboarding
  - Draft SOW with timeline, support SLAs, and rollout plan.
  - Handover to customer success and assign Technical Account Manager (TAM) for enterprise.
